title: Camera domain model (v1)
description: Machine-readable model for the camera-management layer described in docs/research/03-camera-management.md, with the provider registry from docs/research/data/sources.json. The root object is a full domain bundle, so the same file validates an import/seed file and is the reference for the Drizzle tables. Field names are snake_case on purpose: they become column names. docs/architecture.md calls the camera `webcam` and its connection `webcam_source`; this file uses `camera` / `camera_image_source` from the management doc, which is the later, operational model. Where the two disagree, the management doc wins.

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, uppercase. Caltrans and TfL listings give no country; the probe derives it by reverse geocoding.

region_code.description: ISO 3166-2 subdivision code without the country prefix, e.g. "CA" for US-CA.

camera_status.description: unverified: probe passed, no frame stored yet. active: at least one stored frame. paused: frames kept, polling stopped. retired: hidden from map and player, row kept for the audit trail.

paused_reason.description: manual: an operator paused it; only an operator resumes it. provider_failures: failure_count >= 3, recovery is automatic. missing_from_source: an import no longer lists the camera; the operator decides.

probe_status.description: Outcome of the add-camera probe. Each value maps to one message in the UI (docs/research/03-camera-management.md, "Failure messages").

poll_status.description: ok: new bytes stored. unchanged: conditional request or identical sha256, no new frame. Everything else is a failure.

source_kind.description: catalogue_api: a listing endpoint we can bulk import (Digitraffic, Caltrans, TfL). direct_snapshot: a known image URL template. page_scrape: discovery through og:image and friends (foto-webcam). manual: one operator-entered URL.

image_source_kind.description: snapshot is the only kind the v1 poller fetches. hls/mp4/youtube are stored so the player can offer a live tab and are out of scope until the stream phase.

source.description: A provider. Seeded from docs/research/data/sources.json; `id` is the stable slug used by adapters and by camera.source_id.

id.description: Stable slug, also the adapter key. Never rename: camera rows and import runs point at it.

region.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, or a comma-separated list of them, or "worldwide" when the provider has no single region.

attribution_text.description: The credit line a camera of this source must render. Copied onto camera.attribution_text at import time, because the credit is a licence condition and must survive a provider going away.

cadence_seconds.description: The provider's own update cadence. Only an upper bound for polling: the per-camera interval is probed, not copied from here.

camera_count.description: Camera views in the last successful catalogue read. null when the provider has no listing endpoint (PANOMAX).

listing.description: How to read the catalogue. Present only for kind = catalogue_api or page_scrape.

url.description: May contain {district} placeholders; the adapter expands them.

image.description: How to turn a provider camera reference into an image URL. Absent when the URL can only be read from the listing (Caltrans).

request_headers.description: Extra headers sent with every fetch for this camera. Some providers refuse the request without them (Digitraffic wants Accept-Encoding: gzip and a Digitraffic-User). Values may reference secrets by name; never store a token in plain text here.

camera.description: One camera view. A station with several presets is several cameras; the preset id is provider_camera_ref, not the station id.

public_id.description: Short slug used in public URLs. Stable once published.

timezone.description: IANA zone derived from the coordinates by the server; editable because the derived zone is occasionally wrong near a border.

source_id.description: References source.id. Kept as the source slug rather than a UUID so imports and adapters stay readable.

provider_camera_ref.description: The provider's own identifier: the Digitraffic preset id (C0150301), the TfL id (00002.00865), the Caltrans index. Together with source_id it is the import match key and one of the duplicate checks.

page_url.description: Provider page, used as the credit link. foto-webcam.eu allows embedding only if the image links back here.

license_code.description: Short licence identifier. Anything with an attribution obligation must carry attribution_text.

poll_interval_s.description: Per-camera cadence, fixed at save time from the probe and never inferred again. 60 is the floor: no verified source updates faster.

poll_enabled.description: Scheduler flag, independent of status. Failure-driven deactivation leaves it true so a recovered provider resumes on its own; a manual pause leaves it false.

last_ok_at.description: Last poll that produced a new frame. Drives the list default sort (last frame age puts broken cameras first).

failure_count.description: Consecutive failed polls. Reset on success; reaching 3 sets status = paused with paused_reason = provider_failures.

created_by.description: better-auth user id. Null for rows created by an import run rather than a person.

allOf.description: A camera is saved as unverified only after a successful probe; saving an unprobed camera is not allowed.
paused is the only state with a reason, and it always has one.
Failure-driven pause is the one case the scheduler keeps retrying.

camera_image_source.description: One fetchable URL of a camera. A camera may have a snapshot and an HLS stream at once; exactly one row is the primary snapshot.

url.description: Stored normalised: lowercase host, no query, no trailing slash. That normalised form is duplicate check #1.

is_primary.description: The URL the poller fetches and the map shows. At most one primary per camera.

allOf.description: A primary source is a snapshot; a stream is never what the poller fetches.

category.description: Dictionary row behind camera_categories. Windy filters by up to 10 categories with and/or semantics, so this stays a plain many-to-many.

frame.description: One stored image. Bytes live in object storage, never in Postgres; the row carries the key and the hashes. `captured_at` is when the frame was taken (the poll start, or the Last-Modified when the provider gives one), not when the job finished.

storage_key.description: Object-storage key of the original. The same frame is deduped by sha256 per camera.

perceptual_hash.description: Near-duplicate hash, filled by the deferred processing pipeline. Null until then.

poll_attempt.description: Append-only fetch log, pruned after 7 days. A test poll writes here too, outside the schedule. This table answers "why is this camera stuck".

trigger.description: schedule: the normal tick. test: the "Test poll" button. first: the poll queued at save, which is what turns unverified into active.

camera_import_run.description: One bulk import against a catalogue. Every import writes one, so "what changed last night" is answerable. A dry run writes nothing but still records the diff.

removed.description: Counted, never applied: a camera missing from the listing becomes paused with paused_reason = missing_from_source and the operator decides.

errors.description: Per-row failures, kept raw so the diff can be replayed.

probe_report.description: Response of POST /admin/cameras/probe. Not a table: it is the contract between the probe and the add-camera form, and it is what a saved camera's last_probe_* columns are copied from.

final_url.description: After at most 2 redirects. The SSRF check runs again after each hop.

suggested_interval_s.description: From the two-probe comparison: 60 when bytes or validators changed, max-age clamped to 600..3600 when nothing changed and a cache header exists, otherwise 600. Never below 60.

candidates.description: Filled only when the input was a page URL. Ordered by the discovery steps in docs/research/data/url-patterns.json.

duplicate_of_camera_id.description: Set when the frame matches another camera (same normalised URL, same source+ref, or the same sha256). Cases 1-3 block the save, cases 4-5 only warn.

message.description: The exact operator-facing text for a failed probe, e.g. "This URL returns a web page, not an image. Paste the image URL or let the probe search the page."
